# Cale AI Workbench 0.24.16 for Windows

Images could fail with “connection refused” when the local text service was offline, even though the image model and GPU were available. The renderer now proceeds when the optional model listing confirms the service is offline. Other service errors and failed model unloads still surface.

Focusing the image prompt starts loading Python image libraries while you type, when compute and memory are available. Model weights and inference wait for Generate. The unused interpreter is released on leaving Images or after 75 seconds. The Quality preset retains the existing generation and editing behavior. Fast preview uses the installed four-step LCM model for new images and can produce a different composition.

The page now reacts to completed jobs, shares a pending preview verification across refreshes and keeps unchanged history rows in place. When a workspace lacks an image runtime, saved PNGs and imports remain accessible.

## Verification on the owner’s Windows PC

A controlled connection refusal reproduced the old failure. With the same refusal in place, the fixed adapter rendered a 512 × 512 PNG on the RTX 3060. The PNG matched the original successful Quality render byte for byte. Ten native image tests, three text-service regression cases and the history UI regression passed. Over nine idle seconds, the old interface replaced its history six times and the new interface left it in place.
With the same 12-second typing interval, prompt, seed and 512 x 512 dimensions, Generate-to-visible time for Quality went from 17.934 seconds on 0.24.15 to 8.036 and 7.79 seconds on this build. Fast preview took 4.875 and 4.592 seconds under the same conditions. Submitting Quality immediately took 16.391 seconds. The preparation overlaps typing time. The Quality files matched the previous build; Fast preview used a different model.
The desktop checks confirmed that focusing the prompt created no render job, leaving Images released the unused worker, the idle preparation expired, and pausing a claimed job stopped its worker.
